item.title: InSAR from scratch: how radar sees elevation
item.description: This opens a small series on Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), the technique behind most modern maps of volcanic inflation, earthquake deformation, and slow ground subsidence, all derived from satellites that never physically touch the ground. The whole series will build up the pipeline one piece at a time: this post covers where the interferometric phase comes from and why it wraps; later ones will deal with coherence and decorrelation, phase unwrapping, and turning wrapped fringes into an actual displacement time series (SBAS/PSI).
